<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Michael Atiyah
 and Claude LeBrun
</span><span id="id1" class="ltx_note ltx_note_frontmatter ltx_thanks_funding ltx_role_thanks"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_type">thanks: </span>Research supported in part by
the Simons Center for Geometry and Physics.</span></span></span><span id="id2" class="ltx_note ltx_note_frontmatter ltx_thanks_funding ltx_role_thanks"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_type">thanks: </span>Research supported
in part by NSF grant DMS-0905159.</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">We study Einstein metrics on smooth compact <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds
with an edge-cone singularity of specified cone angle along an embedded
<math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold. To do so, we first derive modified versions of the Gauss-Bonnet and signature
theorems for arbitrary
Riemannian <math id="abstract1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds with edge-cone singularities, and then
show that these yield non-trivial obstructions in the
Einstein case.
We then use these integral formulæ to
obtain interesting information regarding
gravitational instantons which arise as limits of such edge-cone manifolds.</p>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Recall <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite> that a Riemannian manifold <math id="S1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,g)</annotation></semantics></math> is said to be
<span id="S1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Einstein</span> if it has constant Ricci curvature; this is equivalent to
requiring that the Ricci tensor <math id="S1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> satisfy</p>
<table id="S1.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S1.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=\lambda g" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=\lambda g</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">for some real number <math id="S1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>, called the Einstein constant of <math id="S1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>.
While one typically requires <math id="S1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> to be a smooth metric on <math id="S1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>,
it is sometimes interesting to consider generalizations where <math id="S1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>
is allowed to have mild singularities. In the Kähler case, beautiful results <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>, <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>, <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite>
have recently been
obtained regarding the situation in which
<math id="S1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> has specific conical singularities along a submanifold of real codimension
<math id="S1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>. Einstein manifolds with such <span id="S1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">edge-cone singularities</span> are the main focus of
the present article.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a smooth <math id="S1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold, and let <math id="S1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma\subset M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma\subset M</annotation></semantics></math> be a smoothly
embedded <math id="S1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(n-2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(n-2)</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold. Near any point <math id="S1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\in\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\in\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, we can thus
find local coordinates <math id="S1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(y^{1},y^{2},x^{1},\ldots,x^{n-2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(y^{1},y^{2},x^{1},\ldots,x^{n-2})</annotation></semantics></math> in which <math id="S1.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>
is given by <math id="S1.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{1}=y^{2}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{1}=y^{2}=0</annotation></semantics></math>. Given any such adapted
coordinate system, we then introduce an associated
<span id="S1.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">transversal polar coordinate</span> system <math id="S1.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\rho,\theta,x^{1},\ldots,x^{n-2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>ρ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>θ</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\rho,\theta,x^{1},\ldots,x^{n-2})</annotation></semantics></math>
by setting <math id="S1.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{1}=\rho\cos\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{1}=\rho\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S1.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{2}=\rho\sin\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{2}=\rho\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math>.
We define a Riemannian edge-cone metric <math id="S1.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> of cone angle
<math id="S1.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi\beta</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S1.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> to be a smooth Riemannian metric
on <math id="S1.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M-\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M-\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> which, for some <math id="S1.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, can be expressed as</p>
<table id="S1.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S1.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g=\bar{g}+\rho^{1+\varepsilon}h" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g=\bar{g}+\rho^{1+\varepsilon}h</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1.1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S1.p2.2" class="ltx_p">near any point of <math id="S1.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>,
where the symmetric tensor field <math id="S1.p2.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S1.p2.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> has infinite conormal regularity
along <math id="S1.p2.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, and where</p>
<table id="S1.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S1.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}=d\rho^{2}+\beta^{2}\rho^{2}(d\theta+u_{j}dx^{j})^{2}+w_{jk}dx^{j}dx^{k}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}=d\rho^{2}+\beta^{2}\rho^{2}(d\theta+u_{j}dx^{j})^{2}+w_{jk}dx^{j}dx^{k}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1.2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S1.p2.3" class="ltx_p">in suitable transversal polar coordinate systems; here <math id="S1.p2.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{jk}(x)dx^{j}dx^{k}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{jk}(x)dx^{j}dx^{k}</annotation></semantics></math>
and <math id="S1.p2.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u_{j}(x)dx^{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>u</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u_{j}(x)dx^{j}</annotation></semantics></math> are a smooth metric and a smooth <math id="S1.p2.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>-form on <math id="S1.p2.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>.
(Our conormal regularity hypothesis means that
the components
of <math id="S1.p2.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S1.p2.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(y,x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(y,x)</annotation></semantics></math> coordinates have infinitely many continuous derivatives with respect to
<math id="S1.p2.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial/\partial x^{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mo rspace="0.055em">/</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mi>j</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial/\partial x^{j}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S1.p2.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\partial/\partial\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mo rspace="0.055em">/</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\partial/\partial\theta</annotation></semantics></math>,
and <math id="S1.p2.m29" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\rho\,\partial/\partial\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>∂</mo><mo rspace="0.055em">/</mo><mo>∂</mo><mi>ρ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho\,\partial/\partial\rho</annotation></semantics></math>.)
Thus, an edge-cone metric <math id="S1.p2.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> behaves like
a smooth metric in directions parallel to <math id="S1.p2.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, but is modelled on
a <math id="S1.p2.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional cone</p>
<p id="S1.p2.4" class="ltx_p ltx_align_center"><span id="S1.p2.4.1" class="ltx_text">
<span id="S1.p2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text"> <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="position:relative; bottom:-55.0pt;"><span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:55.0pt;"></span>    <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:144.7pt;">.</span>    <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:144.7pt;">.</span>    <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:144.7pt;">.</span>    <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.5" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:144.7pt;">.</span>    <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.6" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:144.7pt;">.</span>    <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.7" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:144.7pt;">.</span>    <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.8" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:144.6pt;">.</span>    <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.9" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:142.0pt;">.</span>  <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.42" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:141.9pt;">.</span>  <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.43" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:93.4pt;">.</span>                         <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1758" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:93.4pt;">.</span>                         <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1759" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:93.3pt;">.</span>                          <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1760" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:92.1pt;">.</span>                          <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1761" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:92.0pt;">.</span>                          <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1762" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:91.9pt;">.</span>                          <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1763" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:91.8pt;">.</span>                          <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1764" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:91.7pt;">.</span>                           <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1765" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:91.5pt;">.</span>                           <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1766" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:91.4pt;">.</span>                         <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1767" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:91.3pt;">.</span>                         <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1768" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:91.2pt;">.</span>                          <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1769" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:91.0pt;">.</span>                          <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1770" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:90.9pt;">.</span>                          <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1771" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:90.8pt;">.</span>                          <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1772" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:90.6pt;">.</span>                           <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1773" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:88.2pt;">.</span>                           <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1774" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:88.0pt;">.</span>                           <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1775" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:87.7pt;">.</span>                           <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1776" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:87.4pt;">.</span>                           <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1777" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:87.2pt;">.</span>                           <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1778" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:86.8pt;">.</span>                           <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1779" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:86.5pt;">.</span>                           <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1780" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:86.2pt;">.</span>                           <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1781" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:85.8pt;">.</span>                           <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1782" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:85.5pt;">.</span>                           <span id="S1.p2.4.1.1.1.1783" class="ltx_text ltx_inline-block" style="font-size:50%;width:0.0pt;position:relative; bottom:85.1pt;">.</span></span>                           </span></span></p>
<p id="S1.p2.5" class="ltx_p">in the transverse directions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">If an edge-cone metric
on <math id="S1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>
is
Einstein on <math id="S1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M-\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M-\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, we will call it an Einstein edge-cone metric.
For example, when <math id="S1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta&lt;1/3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta&lt;1/3</annotation></semantics></math>,
any
Kähler-Einstein edge metric of cone angle <math id="S1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi\beta</annotation></semantics></math>, in the sense of
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>, <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>, <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite>, can be shown
<cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>, Proposition 4.3]</cite> to be an Einstein edge-cone metric.
Another
interesting class, with <math id="S1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta=1/p" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>p</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta=1/p</annotation></semantics></math> for some integer
<math id="S1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p\geq 2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p\geq 2</annotation></semantics></math>, is obtained by taking quotients of non-singular Einstein manifolds
by cyclic groups of isometries for which the fixed-point set is purely of codimension <math id="S1.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>2</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2</annotation></semantics></math>.
Some explicit
Einstein edge-cone metrics of much larger cone angle are also
known, as we will see in §<a href="#S5" title="5 Edges and Instantons ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> below.
Because of the wealth of examples produced by such constructions,
it seems entirely reasonable to
limit the present investigation to edge-cone metrics, as defined above.
However, we do so purely
as a matter of exigency. For example, it is remains unknown whether there exist
Einstein metrics with analogous singularities for which the cone angle varies along <math id="S1.p3.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>.
This is an issue which clearly merits thorough exploration.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">The Hitchin-Thorpe inequality <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>, <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>, <a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite> provides an important obstruction to the
existence of Einstein metrics on <math id="S1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds.
If <math id="S1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> is a smooth compact oriented <math id="S1.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold which admits
a smooth Einstein metric <math id="S1.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>, then the Euler characteristic <math id="S1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\chi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>χ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\chi</annotation></semantics></math> and signature
<math id="S1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> must satisfy the two inequalities</p>
<table id="S1.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S1.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(2\chi\pm 3\tau)(M)\geq 0" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>χ</mi></mrow><mo>±</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2\chi\pm 3\tau)(M)\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S1.p4.2" class="ltx_p">because both expressions are represented by Gauss-Bonnet-type integrals
where the integrands become non-negative in the Einstein case.
Note that this inequality hinges on several peculiar features of <math id="S1.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional Riemannian geometry, and that
no analogous obstruction to the existence of Einstein metrics is currently known in
any dimension <math id="S1.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\geq 4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>≥</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq 4</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">In light of the current interest in Einstein metrics with edge-cone singularities,
we believe it is interesting and natural to look for obstructions to their existence
which generalize our understanding of the smooth case. Our main objective
here will be to prove the following version of the Hitchin-Thorpe inequality for edge-cone metrics:</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmmain1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_main">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmmain1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem A</span></span></h6>
<div id="Thmmain1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmmain1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmmain1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmmain1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> be a pair consisting of a smooth compact <math id="Thmmain1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold and
a fixed smoothly embedded compact oriented surface. If <math id="Thmmain1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> admits
an Einstein edge-cone metric with cone angle <math id="Thmmain1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi\beta</annotation></semantics></math> along <math id="Thmmain1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>,
then <math id="Thmmain1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> must satisfy the two inequalities</span></p>
<table id="S1.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S1.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(2\chi\pm 3\tau)(M)\geq(1-\beta)\left(2\chi(\Sigma)\pm(1+\beta)[\Sigma]^{2}\right)~." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>χ</mi></mrow><mo>±</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>χ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>±</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.052em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(2\chi\pm 3\tau)(M)\geq(1-\beta)\left(2\chi(\Sigma)\pm(1+\beta)[\Sigma]^{2}\right)~.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">To show this, we will cast our net a good deal wider. In
§§<a href="#S2" title="2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>–<a href="#S3" title="3 Indices and Orbifolds ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, we prove edge-cone generalizations
of the <math id="S1.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional Gauss-Bonnet and signature formulæ; these results,
Theorems <a href="#S2.Thmthm1" title="Theorem 2.1 ‣ 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a> and <a href="#S2.Thmthm2" title="Theorem 2.2 ‣ 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>,
do not involve the Einstein condition,
but rather apply to arbitrary edge-cone
metrics on compact <math id="S1.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifolds. We then zero in on the Einstein case
in §<a href="#S4" title="4 Edges and Einstein Metrics ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, proving Theorem <a href="#Thmmain1" title="Theorem A ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>
and exploring some of its implications.
But Theorems <a href="#S2.Thmthm1" title="Theorem 2.1 ‣ 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a> and <a href="#S2.Thmthm2" title="Theorem 2.2 ‣ 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a> have broader ramifications.
In §<a href="#S5" title="5 Edges and Instantons ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>,
we apply them to the study of some explicit self-dual edge-cone metrics, and explore
the remarkable way that certain gravitational
instantons arise as limits of edge-cone manifolds as <math id="S1.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta\to 0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Curvature Integrals and Topology</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The Euler characteristic <math id="S2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\chi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>χ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\chi</annotation></semantics></math> and signature <math id="S2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau</annotation></semantics></math> of a smooth compact <math id="S2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold <math id="S2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>
may both be calculated by choosing any smooth Riemannian metric <math id="S2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>,
and then integrating appropriate universal quadratic polynomials
in the curvature of <math id="S2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>. When <math id="S2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> has an edge-cone singularity, however,
correction terms must be introduced in order to compensate for the singularity
of the metric along the given surface <math id="S2.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma\subset M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma\subset M</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmthm1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_thm">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmthm1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 2.1</span></span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmthm1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a smooth compact oriented <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold, and
let <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma\subset M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma\subset M</annotation></semantics></math> be a smooth compact oriented embedded surface. Then,
for any edge-cone metric <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> with cone angle <math id="S2.Thmthm1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi\beta</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S2.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\chi(M)-(1-\beta)\chi(\Sigma)=\frac{1}{8\pi^{2}}\int_{M}\left(\frac{s^{2}}{24}+|W|^{2}-\frac{|\mathring{r}|^{2}}{2}\right)d\mu~." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>χ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>χ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0em">∫</mo><mi>M</mi></msub><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>24</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.330em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\chi(M)-(1-\beta)\chi(\Sigma)=\frac{1}{8\pi^{2}}\int_{M}\left(\frac{s^{2}}{24}+|W|^{2}-\frac{|\mathring{r}|^{2}}{2}\right)d\mu~.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2.1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmthm2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_thm">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmthm2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Theorem 2.2</span></span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmthm2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmthm2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmthm2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S2.Thmthm2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math> be a smooth compact oriented <math id="S2.Thmthm2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold, and
let <math id="S2.Thmthm2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma\subset M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma\subset M</annotation></semantics></math> be a smooth compact oriented embedded surface.
Then,
for any edge-cone metric <math id="S2.Thmthm2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S2.Thmthm2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> with cone angle <math id="S2.Thmthm2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi\beta</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S2.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tau(M)-\frac{1}{3}(1-\beta^{2})[\Sigma]^{2}=\frac{1}{12\pi^{2}}\int_{M}\left(|W_{+}|^{2}-|W_{-}|^{2}\right)d\mu~." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>τ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>3</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msup><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mn>12</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mo rspace="0em">∫</mo><mi>M</mi></msub><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mo>−</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0em">𝑑</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0.330em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tau(M)-\frac{1}{3}(1-\beta^{2})[\Sigma]^{2}=\frac{1}{12\pi^{2}}\int_{M}\left(|W_{+}|^{2}-|W_{-}|^{2}\right)d\mu~.</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Here <math id="S2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="s" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>s</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">s</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathring{r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathring{r}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>W</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math> are the scalar curvature, trace-free Ricci tensor,
and Weyl curvature of <math id="S2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>, while <math id="S2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{+}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{-}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mo>−</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{-}</annotation></semantics></math> are the self-dual and
anti-self-dual parts of <math id="S2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>W</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math>,
and <math id="S2.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d\mu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d\mu</annotation></semantics></math> is the metric
volume <math id="S2.p2.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-form. We follow standard conventions <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite> by defining</p>
<table id="S2.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathring{r}|^{2}:=\mathring{r}_{jk}\mathring{r}^{jk}~,\hskip 36.135pt|W|^{2}:=\frac{1}{4}W_{jk\ell m}W^{jk\ell m}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>:=</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="3.777em">,</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>W</mi><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>m</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathring{r}|^{2}:=\mathring{r}_{jk}\mathring{r}^{jk}~,\hskip 36.135pt|W|^{2}:=\frac{1}{4}W_{jk\ell m}W^{jk\ell m}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where the factor of <math id="S2.p2.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1/4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1/4</annotation></semantics></math> arises from treating <math id="S2.p2.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>W</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W</annotation></semantics></math> as an element of
<math id="S2.p2.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Lambda^{2}\otimes\Lambda^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Λ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Lambda^{2}\otimes\Lambda^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>; the point-wise norms of <math id="S2.p2.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{\pm}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mo>±</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{\pm}</annotation></semantics></math> are defined
analogously, so that</p>
<table id="S2.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|W|^{2}=|W_{+}|^{2}+|W_{-}|^{2}~." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>W</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mo>−</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|W|^{2}=|W_{+}|^{2}+|W_{-}|^{2}~.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p2.3" class="ltx_p">The expression <math id="S2.p2.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="[\Sigma]^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">[\Sigma]^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>
denotes the self-intersection of the homology class of <math id="S2.p2.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> in
<math id="S2.p2.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{2}(M)\cong H^{2}(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≅</mo><mrow><msup><mi>H</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{2}(M)\cong H^{2}(M)</annotation></semantics></math>, and coincides with the Euler class of the normal bundle of
<math id="S2.p2.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, paired with the fundamental cycle of the surface.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We first discovered Theorems <a href="#S2.Thmthm1" title="Theorem 2.1 ‣ 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a> and <a href="#S2.Thmthm2" title="Theorem 2.2 ‣ 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>
in the context of global-quotient orbifolds, and we outline a method for deducing the general case
from this special one in §<a href="#S3" title="3 Indices and Orbifolds ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> below.
Another workable strategy, which we leave to the interested reader,
would be to apply the Gauss-Bonnet and
signature theorems with boundary <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite> to the complement of a tubular neighborhood
of <math id="S2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma\in M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma\in M</annotation></semantics></math>, and then take limits as the radius of the tube tends to zero.
However, we will instead begin here by giving a complete and
self-contained proof by yet a third
method, of a purely differential-geometric flavor.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">For this purpose, observe that, by taking linear combinations,
equations
(<a href="#S2.E1" title="In Theorem 2.1 ‣ 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>) and (<a href="#S2.E2" title="In Theorem 2.2 ‣ 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>) are equivalent to the pair of equations</p>

<p id="S2.p4.2" class="ltx_p">provided we define the <span id="S2.p4.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">defects</span> <math id="S2.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dft_{\pm}(M,\Sigma,\beta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>def</mi><mo>±</mo></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dft_{\pm}(M,\Sigma,\beta)</annotation></semantics></math> to be</p>

</table>
<p id="S2.p4.3" class="ltx_p">However, equations (<a href="#S2.E3" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>)
and (<a href="#S2.E4" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.4</span></a>) are interchanged by simply reversing the orientation of <math id="S2.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>.
To prove Propositions <a href="#S2.Thmthm1" title="Theorem 2.1 ‣ 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a> and <a href="#S2.Thmthm2" title="Theorem 2.2 ‣ 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>, it therefore suffices to
prove that (<a href="#S2.E3" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>) holds for any edge-cone metric on <math id="S2.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> with cone angle <math id="S2.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi\beta</annotation></semantics></math>,
with defect <math id="S2.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dft_{+}(\Sigma,\beta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>def</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dft_{+}(\Sigma,\beta)</annotation></semantics></math> given by (<a href="#S2.E5" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a>).
We now simplify the problem further by showing that, for each
<math id="S2.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>, it suffices to check
that (<a href="#S2.E3" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>) holds for a single edge-cone metric on <math id="S2.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> of
cone angle <math id="S2.p4.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi\beta</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmlem1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_lem">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmlem1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Lemma 2.1</span></span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmlem1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmlem1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmlem1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="S2.Thmlem1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> be a smooth compact oriented <math id="S2.Thmlem1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold equipped with
a smooth compact oriented embedded surface, and let <math id="S2.Thmlem1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math> be a positive real number.
Fix two real constants
<math id="S2.Thmlem1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="a" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>a</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.Thmlem1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math>, and consider the formula for <math id="S2.Thmlem1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(a\chi+b\tau)(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>χ</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(a\chi+b\tau)(M)</annotation></semantics></math> obtained by
taking the corresponding linear combination of (<a href="#S2.E1" title="In Theorem 2.1 ‣ 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>) and (<a href="#S2.E2" title="In Theorem 2.2 ‣ 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>).
If this formula holds for one edge-cone metric on <math id="S2.Thmlem1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> of cone angle <math id="S2.Thmlem1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi\beta</annotation></semantics></math>,
it also holds for
every other edge-cone metric on <math id="S2.Thmlem1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>
of the same cone angle.</span></p>
</div>
</div>

the <math id="S2.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-forms</p>
