<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>=</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S2.Ex11.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\displaystyle-\mathcal{R}_{jk[bc}\nabla^{j}\dot{g}^{k}_{d]}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi>b</mi><mi>c</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>j</mi></msup><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><msup><mrow></mrow><mi>k</mi></msup><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle-\mathcal{R}_{jk[bc}\nabla^{j}\dot{g}^{k}_{d]}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p5.7" class="ltx_p">which obviously satisfy</p>
<table id="S2.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\phi|,|\psi|\leq|\mathcal{R}||\nabla\dot{g}|~." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>ϕ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>ψ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mo rspace="0.167em">∇</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover></mrow><mo rspace="0.052em" stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\phi|,|\psi|\leq|\mathcal{R}||\nabla\dot{g}|~.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2.6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Now we have defined an edge-cone metric <math id="S2.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S2.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> of cone angle <math id="S2.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi\beta</annotation></semantics></math> to be
a tensor field which is smooth on <math id="S2.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M-\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M-\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, and which can be written
as <math id="S2.p6.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}+\rho^{1+\varepsilon}h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}+\rho^{1+\varepsilon}h</annotation></semantics></math> for some <math id="S2.p6.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S2.p6.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math>
has infinite conormal regularity at <math id="S2.p6.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, and where the background metric <math id="S2.p6.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}</annotation></semantics></math>
takes
the form</p>
<table id="S2.Ex12" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}=d\rho^{2}+\beta^{2}\rho^{2}(d\theta+\nu)^{2}+g_{\Sigma}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msup><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>ν</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}=d\rho^{2}+\beta^{2}\rho^{2}(d\theta+\nu)^{2}+g_{\Sigma}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p6.2" class="ltx_p">in suitable transverse polar coordinates, where <math id="S2.p6.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p6.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\Sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\Sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> are the pull-backs to a tubular neighborhood
of <math id="S2.p6.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> of a smooth <math id="S2.p6.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>-form and a smooth Riemannian metric on <math id="S2.p6.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>.
While <math id="S2.p6.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p6.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>θ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\theta</annotation></semantics></math> can be related to a system of smooth coordinates
<math id="S2.p6.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(y^{1},y^{2},x^{1},x^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(y^{1},y^{2},x^{1},x^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> by <math id="S2.p6.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{1}=\rho\cos\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{1}=\rho\cos\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.p6.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y^{2}=\rho\sin\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>y</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y^{2}=\rho\sin\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, we now
set <math id="S2.p6.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{\theta}=\beta\theta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{\theta}=\beta\theta</annotation></semantics></math>, and
introduce new local coordinates on transversely
wedge-shaped regions by setting <math id="S2.p6.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{y}^{1}=\rho\cos\tilde{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mn>1</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>cos</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{y}^{1}=\rho\cos\tilde{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S2.p6.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{y}^{2}=\rho\sin\tilde{\theta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>θ</mi><mo>~</mo></mover></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{y}^{2}=\rho\sin\tilde{\theta}</annotation></semantics></math>. In these coordinates, <math id="S2.p6.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}</annotation></semantics></math> simply appears to
be a smooth metric with <math id="S2.p6.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{SO}(2)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>𝐒𝐎</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{SO}(2)</annotation></semantics></math>-symmetry around <math id="S2.p6.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, while the tensor
field <math id="S2.p6.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>h</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> still has the same infinite conormal regularity as before. Thus the
first derivatives of the components of <math id="S2.p6.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S2.p6.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\tilde{y},x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\tilde{y},x)</annotation></semantics></math> coordinates
are smooth plus terms of order
<math id="S2.p6.m29" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho^{\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mi>ε</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho^{\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math>, while the second derivatives are no worse than
<math id="S2.p6.m30" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho^{-1+\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho^{-1+\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math>. Since <math id="S2.p6.m31" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{-1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{-1}</annotation></semantics></math> is also continuous across <math id="S2.p6.m32" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, it follows
that the Christoffel symbols <math id="S2.p6.m33" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Gamma^{j}_{k\ell}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi mathvariant="normal">Γ</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">ℓ</mi></mrow><mi>j</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Gamma^{j}_{k\ell}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S2.p6.m34" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> in <math id="S2.p6.m35" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\tilde{y},x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\tilde{y},x)</annotation></semantics></math> coordinates are bounded,
and that the norm <math id="S2.p6.m36" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\mathcal{R}|_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mi>g</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\mathcal{R}|_{g}</annotation></semantics></math> of the curvature tensor at worst blows up
like <math id="S2.p6.m37" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho^{-1+\varepsilon}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho^{-1+\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Given two edge-cone
metrics <math id="S2.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S2.p7.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> of the same cone angle <math id="S2.p7.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi\beta</annotation></semantics></math>,
we first apply a diffeomorphism to <math id="S2.p7.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> in order to arrange that the
two choices of radius functions <math id="S2.p7.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ρ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho</annotation></semantics></math> and identifications
of the normal bundle of <math id="S2.p7.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> with a tubular neighborhood
agree; thus, without interfering with our curvature integrals, we can assume that
the two given choices of <math id="S2.p7.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{g}</annotation></semantics></math> differ only insofar as they involve different choices of
<math id="S2.p7.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ν</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nu</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p7.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\Sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\Sigma}</annotation></semantics></math>. The <math id="S2.p7.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math>-parameter family <math id="S2.p7.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{{\zap t}}=(1-{\zap t})g+{\zap t}g^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>g</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{{\zap t}}=(1-{\zap t})g+{\zap t}g^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="S2.p7.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\zap t}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\zap t}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> is then a family of edge-cone metrics on <math id="S2.p7.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math>
of fixed cone angle <math id="S2.p7.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi\beta</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p8.1" class="ltx_p">We will now show that
<math id="S2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int_{M}\Phi_{g_{\zap t}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∫</mo><mi>M</mi></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{M}\Phi_{g_{\zap t}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int_{M}\Psi_{g_{\zap t}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mo>∫</mo><mi>M</mi></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{M}\Psi_{g_{\zap t}}</annotation></semantics></math> are independent of <math id="S2.p8.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\zap t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\zap t}</annotation></semantics></math>.
To see this, let us write</p>
<table id="S2.Ex13" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\frac{d}{dt}\Phi_{g_{\zap t}}=d\phi_{{\zap t}}\qquad\qquad\frac{d}{dt}\Psi_{g_{\zap t}}=d\psi_{{\zap t}}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mspace style="width:4em;" width="4em"></mspace><mrow><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi></msub></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{d}{dt}\Phi_{g_{\zap t}}=d\phi_{{\zap t}}\qquad\qquad\frac{d}{dt}\Psi_{g_{\zap t}}=d\psi_{{\zap t}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p8.2" class="ltx_p">as above, and notice that (<a href="#S2.E6" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.6</span></a>) tells us that</p>
<table id="S2.Ex14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|\phi_{\zap t}|,|\psi_{\zap t}|\leq C\rho^{-1+\varepsilon}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>ρ</mi><mrow><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mi>ε</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|\phi_{\zap t}|,|\psi_{\zap t}|\leq C\rho^{-1+\varepsilon}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p8.3" class="ltx_p">for some positive constants <math id="S2.p8.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p8.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ε</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math> determined by <math id="S2.p8.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p8.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>,
since
the first derivatives of <math id="S2.p8.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dot{g}=g^{\prime}-g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>g</mi><mo>˙</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>−</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dot{g}=g^{\prime}-g</annotation></semantics></math>
in <math id="S2.p8.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(\tilde{y},x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>y</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>,</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(\tilde{y},x)</annotation></semantics></math> coordinates are bounded.
Now let <math id="S2.p8.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M_{\delta}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>δ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M_{\delta}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the complement of a tube <math id="S2.p8.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\rho&lt;\delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ρ</mi><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>δ</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\rho&lt;\delta</annotation></semantics></math> around
<math id="S2.p8.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>. Then</p>
<table id="S2.Ex15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|\frac{d}{dt}\int_{M_{\delta}}\Phi_{g_{\zap t}}\right|=\left|\int_{M_{\delta}}\frac{d}{dt}{\Phi}_{g_{\zap lspace="0em">∫</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>δ</mi></msub></msub><mrow><mfrac><mi>d</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi></msub></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em">∫</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>δ</mi></msub></mrow></msub><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mi lspace="0em">∂</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>δ</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>g</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mover <p id="S2.p8.4" class="ltx_p">for some <math id="S2.p8.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\zap t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\zap t}</annotation></semantics></math>-independent constant <math id="S2.p8.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mi>C</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{C}</annotation></semantics></math>. Integrating in <math id="S2.p8.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\zap t}\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\zap t}\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math>, we thus have</p>
<table id="S2.Ex16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\left|\int_{M_{\delta}}\Phi_{g^{\prime}}-\int_{M_{\delta}}\Phi_{g}\right|&lt;\tilde{C}\delta^{\varepsilon}~," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo>|</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0em">∫</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>δ</mi></msub></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">−</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∫</mo><msub><mi>M</mi><mi>δ</mi></msub></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>|</mo></mrow><mo>&lt;</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mi>C</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>δ</mi><mi>ε</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\left|\int_{M_{\delta}}\Phi_{g^{\prime}}-\int_{M_{\delta}}\Phi_{g}\right|&lt;\tilde{C}\delta^{\varepsilon}~,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p8.5" class="ltx_p">and taking the limit <math id="S2.p8.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\delta\to 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>δ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\delta\to 0</annotation></semantics></math> therefore yields</p>
<table id="S2.Ex17" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int_{M}\Phi_{g^{\prime}}=\int_{M}\Phi_{g}~." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∫</mo><mi>M</mi></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∫</mo><mi>M</mi></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Φ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{M}\Phi_{g^{\prime}}=\int_{M}\Phi_{g}~.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p8.6" class="ltx_p">Replacing <math id="S2.p8.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\phi_{\zap t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ϕ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\phi_{\zap t}</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="S2.p8.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\psi_{\zap t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>ψ</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝓉</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\psi_{\zap t}</annotation></semantics></math> similarly proves that
<math id="S2.p8.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int_{M}\Psi_{g^{\prime}}=\int_{M}\Psi_{g}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∫</mo><mi>M</mi></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo>∫</mo><mi>M</mi></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Ψ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{M}\Psi_{g^{\prime}}=\int_{M}\Psi_{g}</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, if a given linear combination of
(<a href="#S2.E1" title="In Theorem 2.1 ‣ 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.1</span></a>) and (<a href="#S2.E2" title="In Theorem 2.2 ‣ 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.2</span></a>) is true for some edge-cone metric
<math id="S2.p8.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>, it is also true for any other edge-cone metric <math id="S2.p8.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>g</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> of the same cone angle.
 <span id="S2.p8.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="position:relative; bottom:-2.0pt;"><span class="ltx_rule" style="width:7.0pt;height:8.0pt;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span></span>

<br class="ltx_break"></p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p9.1" class="ltx_p">We may thus focus our attention on proving (<a href="#S2.E3" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>) for some particular edge-cone metric
for each <math id="S2.p9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p9.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>β</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. For any given metric,
let us therefore adopt the provisional notation</p>
<table id="S2.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Upsilon=\left(\frac{s^{2}}{24}+2|W_{+}|^{2}-\frac{|\mathring{r}|^{2}}{2}\right)d\mu" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>24</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mfrac><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Upsilon=\left(\frac{s^{2}}{24}+2|W_{+}|^{2}-\frac{|\mathring{r}|^{2}}{2}\right)d\mu</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2.7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p9.2" class="ltx_p">for the <math id="S2.p9.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-form appearing as the integrand in (<a href="#S2.E3" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>).
If <math id="S2.p9.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> is an edge-cone metric of cone angle <math id="S2.p9.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi\beta</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S2.p9.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> and if
<math id="S2.p9.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> is a smooth metric on <math id="S2.p9.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>M</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M</annotation></semantics></math>, then (<a href="#S2.E3" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>) is equivalent to the claim
that</p>
<table id="S2.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int_{M}\left(\Upsilon_{g}-\Upsilon_{g_{0}}\right)=-4\pi^{2}\dft_{+}(\Sigma,\beta)~," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∫</mo><mi>M</mi></msub><mrow><mo lspace="0em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mi>def</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo rspace="0.330em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{M}\left(\Upsilon_{g}-\Upsilon_{g_{0}}\right)=-4\pi^{2}\dft_{+}(\Sigma,\beta)~,</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2.8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p9.3" class="ltx_p">since integral of <math id="S2.p9.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Upsilon_{g_{0}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Upsilon_{g_{0}}</annotation></semantics></math> is <math id="S2.p9.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4\pi^{2}(2\chi+3\tau)(M)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>χ</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\pi^{2}(2\chi+3\tau)(M)</annotation></semantics></math>
by the
standard Gauss-Bonnet and signature theorems.
Of course, if we can actually arrange for
<math id="S2.p9.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p9.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> to exactly agree on the complement of some
tubular neighborhood <math id="S2.p9.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S2.p9.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, this reduces to the statement that</p>
<table id="S2.Ex18" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int_{{\mathcal{V}}-\Sigma}\left(\Upsilon_{g}-\Upsilon_{g_{0}}\right)=-4\pi^{2}\dft_{+}(\Sigma,\beta)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∫</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo lspace="0em">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><msub><mi>def</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>β</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{{\mathcal{V}}-\Sigma}\left(\Upsilon_{g}-\Upsilon_{g_{0}}\right)=-4\pi^{2}\dft_{+}(\Sigma,\beta)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p9.4" class="ltx_p">since <math id="S2.p9.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Upsilon_{g}-\Upsilon_{g_{0}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Upsilon_{g}-\Upsilon_{g_{0}}</annotation></semantics></math> is then supported in <math id="S2.p9.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\mathcal{V}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\mathcal{V}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and
<math id="S2.p9.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> has <math id="S2.p9.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-dimensional measure zero.
In the proof that follows, we will not only choose <math id="S2.p9.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S2.p9.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> to be related
in this manner, but also arrange for both of them to be Kähler on <math id="S2.p9.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}</annotation></semantics></math>. Now</p>
<table id="S2.Ex19" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex19.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|W_{+}|^{2}=\frac{s^{2}}{24}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>24</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|W_{+}|^{2}=\frac{s^{2}}{24}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p9.5" class="ltx_p">for any Kähler metric on a compatibly oriented
<math id="S2.p9.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>4</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4</annotation></semantics></math>-manifold, so (<a href="#S2.E7" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.7</span></a>) simplifies in the Kähler case to become</p>
<table id="S2.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Upsilon=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{s^{2}}{4}-|\mathring{r}|^{2}\right)d\mu=\varrho\wedge\varrho" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Υ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>s</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mo>−</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>r</mi><mo>̊</mo></mover><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>μ</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>ϱ</mi><mo>∧</mo><mi>ϱ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Upsilon=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{s^{2}}{4}-|\mathring{r}|^{2}\right)d\mu=\varrho\wedge\varrho</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2.9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p9.6" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.p9.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varrho" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ϱ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varrho</annotation></semantics></math> is the Ricci form. This will reduce the problem to showing that</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\int_{{\mathcal{V}}-\Sigma}\left(\varrho_{g}\wedge\varrho_{g}-\varrho_{g_{0}}\wedge\varrho_{g_{0}}\right)=-4\pi^{2}(1-\beta)\left[2\chi(\Sigma)+(1+\beta)[\Sigma]^{2}\right]" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∫</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mo>−</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><mo lspace="0em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub><mo>∧</mo><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub></mrow><mo>∧</mo><msub><mi>ϱ</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>χ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\int_{{\mathcal{V}}-\Sigma}\left(\varrho_{g}\wedge\varrho_{g}-\varrho_{g_{0}}\wedge\varrho_{g_{0}}\right)=-4\pi^{2}(1-\beta)\left[2\chi(\Sigma)+(1+\beta)[\Sigma]^{2}\right]</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2.10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p9.7" class="ltx_p">and, by exploiting some
key properties of the Ricci form, this will follow by an application of Stokes’ theorem.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p10" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p10.1" class="ltx_p">Our choice of <math id="S2.p10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{0}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{0}</annotation></semantics></math> will involve an auxiliary function
<math id="S2.p10.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(t)</annotation></semantics></math>, which we will now construct. First let <math id="S2.p10.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f:{\mathbb{R}}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>ℝ</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mo>+</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f:{\mathbb{R}}\to{\mathbb{R}}^{+}</annotation></semantics></math> be a smooth
positive function with</p>
<table id="S2.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<p id="S2.p10.3" class="ltx_p">We next define <math id="S2.p10.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(t)</annotation></semantics></math> up to a constant of integration by setting</p>

<p id="S2.p10.4" class="ltx_p">where this definition of course entails that <math id="S2.p10.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F^{\prime}\equiv 1/\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>F</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>≡</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F^{\prime}\equiv 1/\beta</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S2.p10.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\leq 1/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\leq 1/2</annotation></semantics></math>.
Because <math id="S2.p10.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> consequently solves the differential equation</p>

</table>
<p id="S2.p10.5" class="ltx_p">it follows that the smooth, rotationally symmetric metric on the <math id="S2.p10.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\zeta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ζ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\zeta</annotation></semantics></math>-plane <math id="S2.p10.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbb{C}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ℂ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbb{C}</annotation></semantics></math>
with Kähler form</p>
<table id="S2.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2.14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p10.6" class="ltx_p">is Euclidean near the origin and coincides with a standard cone of perimeter angle <math id="S2.p10.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi\beta</annotation></semantics></math>
outside the unit disk. Condition (<a href="#S2.E11" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.11</span></a>) guarantees that <math id="S2.p10.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F^{\prime}(1)=1/\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>F</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>/</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F^{\prime}(1)=1/\beta</annotation></semantics></math>,
so inspection of the differential equation (<a href="#S2.E13" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.13</span></a>) tells us that</p>
<table id="S2.Ex21" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex21.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F(t)=\frac{t^{\beta}}{\beta^{2}}+B" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><msup><mi>t</mi><mi>β</mi></msup><msup><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F(t)=\frac{t^{\beta}}{\beta^{2}}+B</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p10.7" class="ltx_p">for all <math id="S2.p10.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t\geq 1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>≥</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t\geq 1</annotation></semantics></math>, for a constant of integration <math id="S2.p10.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> which we may take to vanish.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.Thmprop1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_prop">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="S2.Thmprop1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 2.1</span></span></h6>
<div id="S2.Thmprop1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.Thmprop1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.Thmprop1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For any compact oriented pair <math id="S2.Thmprop1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M^{4},\Sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>M</mi><mn>4</mn></msup><mo>,</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M^{4},\Sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math> and any positive real number
<math id="S2.Thmprop1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>β</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta</annotation></semantics></math>, there is an edge-cone metric <math id="S2.Thmprop1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S2.Thmprop1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(M,\Sigma)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>M</mi><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(M,\Sigma)</annotation></semantics></math> with cone angle <math id="S2.Thmprop1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\pi\beta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>π</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>β</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\pi\beta</annotation></semantics></math>
such that </span>(<a href="#S2.E3" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.3</span></a>)<span id="S2.Thmprop1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic"> holds, with defect <math id="S2.Thmprop1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\dft_{+}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>def</mi><mo>+</mo></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\dft_{+}</annotation></semantics></math> given by </span>(<a href="#S2.E5" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.5</span></a>)<span id="S2.Thmprop1.p1.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S2.p11" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p11.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S2.p11.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proof.</span>
Choose any metric <math id="S2.p11.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\Sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\Sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S2.p11.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, and
remember that, in conjunction with the given orientation, its conformal class
makes <math id="S2.p11.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> into a
compact complex curve; in particular, the area form <math id="S2.p11.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S2.p11.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g_{\Sigma}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g_{\Sigma}</annotation></semantics></math> then becomes
its Kähler form. Let <math id="S2.p11.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varpi:E\to\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϖ</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varpi:E\to\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> be the normal bundle of
<math id="S2.p11.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma\subset M" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mo>⊂</mo><mi>M</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma\subset M</annotation></semantics></math>, and choose an inner product <math id="S2.p11.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\langle~,~\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0.330em" stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mo rspace="0.497em">,</mo><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle~,~\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S2.p11.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math>;
this reduces the structure group of <math id="S2.p11.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> to <math id="S2.p11.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{SO}(2)=\mathbf{U}(1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>𝐒𝐎</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>𝐔</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{SO}(2)=\mathbf{U}(1)</annotation></semantics></math>, and so makes
it into a complex line bundle. Next, we choose
a <math id="S2.p11.m12" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\langle~,~\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0.330em" stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mo rspace="0.497em">,</mo><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle~,~\rangle</annotation></semantics></math>-compatible connection <math id="S2.p11.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∇</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S2.p11.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> whose
curvature is a constant multiple of <math id="S2.p11.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> on each connected component of <math id="S2.p11.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>. Viewing <math id="S2.p11.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla^{0,1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mo>∇</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla^{0,1}</annotation></semantics></math> as a <math id="S2.p11.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\partial}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mover accent="true"><mo>∂</mo><mo>¯</mo></mover><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\partial}</annotation></semantics></math>-operator on <math id="S2.p11.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> then makes
it into a holomorphic line bundle over <math id="S2.p11.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>, in a unique manner that
identifies <math id="S2.p11.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∇</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla</annotation></semantics></math> with the Chern connection induced by <math id="S2.p11.m22" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\langle~,~\rangle" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0.330em" stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mo rspace="0.497em">,</mo><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\langle~,~\rangle</annotation></semantics></math> and the
holomorphic structure. Thus
the curvature of <math id="S2.p11.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\nabla" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∇</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\nabla</annotation></semantics></math>
is <math id="S2.p11.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-i\kappa\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>α</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-i\kappa\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>, where the locally constant real-valued function <math id="S2.p11.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>κ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa</annotation></semantics></math>
takes the value</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<p id="S2.p11.2" class="ltx_p">on the <math id="S2.p11.m26" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j^{\rm th}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>j</mi><mi>th</mi></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j^{\rm th}</annotation></semantics></math> connected component
<math id="S2.p11.m27" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S2.p11.m28" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p12" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p12.1" class="ltx_p">We will let <math id="S2.p12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t:E\to{\mathbb{R}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>E</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><mi>ℝ</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t:E\to{\mathbb{R}}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the square-norm function <math id="S2.p12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t(v)=\|v\|^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>v</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t(v)=\|v\|^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>, and
our computations will involve various closed <math id="S2.p12.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1,1)</annotation></semantics></math>-forms expressed as
<math id="S2.p12.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\partial\bar{\partial}u(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mo lspace="0em">∂</mo><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\partial\bar{\partial}u(t)</annotation></semantics></math> for various functions <math id="S2.p12.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="u(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>u</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">u(t)</annotation></semantics></math>.
To understand such expressions explicitly, first choose
a local coordinate <math id="S2.p12.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>z</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S2.p12.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> so that near the origin</p>

<p id="S2.p12.2" class="ltx_p">and then choose a local trivialization
of <math id="S2.p12.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math> determined by a local holomorphic section <math id="S2.p12.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\xi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ξ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\xi</annotation></semantics></math> with vanishing covariant derivative and unit norm at the origin. Then the function <math id="S2.p12.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{\zap h}:=\|\xi\|^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝒽</mi><mo>:=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mi>ξ</mi><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{\zap h}:=\|\xi\|^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> satisfies</p>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S2.p12.3" class="ltx_p">because <math id="S2.p12.m11" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="-\partial\bar{\partial}\log{\zap h}=-i\kappa\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">−</mo><mo>∂</mo><mover accent="true"><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">∂</mo><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>log</mi><mi class="ltx_font_mathscript">𝒽</mi><mo rspace="0em">=</mo><mo lspace="0em">−</mo><mi>i</mi><mi>κ</mi><mi>α</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-\partial\bar{\partial}\log{\zap h}=-i\kappa\alpha</annotation></semantics></math> is the curvature
of <math id="S2.p12.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, introducing a fiber coordinate <math id="S2.p12.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\zeta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ζ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\zeta</annotation></semantics></math> associated with the local trivialization,
then, near the <math id="S2.p12.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\zeta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ζ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\zeta</annotation></semantics></math>-axis which represents the fiber over <math id="S2.p12.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z=0</annotation></semantics></math>, we have</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S2.Ex25.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\partial\bar{\partial}u(t)=i(tu^{\prime})^{\prime}d\zeta\wedge d\bar{\zeta}-i\kappa(tu^{\prime})dz\wedge d\bar{z}+O(|z|)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mo lspace="0em">∂</mo><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>′</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>ζ</mi></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>ζ</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>κ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>u</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>∧</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mover accent="true"><mi>z</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>O</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>z</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\partial\bar{\partial}u(t)=i(tu^{\prime})^{\prime}d\zeta\wedge d\bar{\zeta}-i\kappa(tu^{\prime})dz\wedge d\bar{z}+O(|z|)</annotation></semantics></math></td>

</table>
<p id="S2.p12.4" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S2.p12.m16" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t=|\zeta|^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mi>ζ</mi><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t=|\zeta|^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> along the <math id="S2.p12.m17" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\zeta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ζ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\zeta</annotation></semantics></math>-axis. Since the chosen point <math id="S2.p12.m18" class="ltx_Math" alttext="z=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>z</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">z=0</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S2.p12.m19" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Sigma" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Σ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Sigma</annotation></semantics></math> was in fact
arbitrary, this calculation of course actually
computes <math id="S2.p12.m20" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\partial\bar{\partial}u(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mrow><mover accent="true"><mo lspace="0em">∂</mo><mo>¯</mo></mover><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>u</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\partial\bar{\partial}u(t)</annotation></semantics></math> along <span id="S2.p12.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">any</span> fiber.
For example, consider the <math id="S2.p12.m21" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(1,1)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(1,1)</annotation></semantics></math>-forms</p>

<p id="S2.p12.5" class="ltx_p">and</p>

<p id="S2.p12.6" class="ltx_p">on <math id="S2.p12.m22" class="ltx_Math" alttext="E" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>E</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">E</annotation></semantics></math>, for some large positive constant <math id="S2.p12.m23" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>λ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S2.p12.m24" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> is given by (<a href="#S2.E11" title="In 2 Curvature Integrals and Topology ‣ Curvature, Cones, and Characteristic Numbers" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2.11</span></a>). Explicitly, these are given
along the <math id="S2.p12.m25" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\zeta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ζ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\zeta</annotation></semantics></math>-axis of our coordinate system by</p>
